question: Before deleting an EC2 instance, an operator needs a reusable point-in-time copy of its EBS volume. Which action preserves that block data?

answers.text: Create an Amazon S3 object lifecycle rule
answers.explanation: S3 lifecycle rules transition or expire S3 objects. They do not capture the blocks of an attached EBS volume.
FSx creates a managed file system for workloads such as Windows file shares or Lustre. It does not snapshot an existing EBS block volume.
An EBS snapshot is a point-in-time backup of an EBS volume. A new volume can later be created from that snapshot independently of the original EC2 instance.

answers.text: Mount the volume through Amazon EFS
answers.explanation: EFS is a separate shared NFS file service. Mounting EFS does not make a point-in-time copy of an EBS volume.
